She closed with 'thank you so much for your help, I really appreciate it.'
coaching_note: This was a warm intake, not a sales call — he collected a great inventory and then gave away every closing lever. A repeat customer with a confirmed September 2nd date told him she had a good experience last time and was ready to go; instead of quoting her on the phone and asking to lock the date, he ended with 'you'll get an email in twenty or 25 minutes... have a day or two to think on it.' Jespah needs to run the back half of the script live: hourly rate and what's included, No Worries coverage (she is moving glass, marble, and mirrors), the 2.5-hour minimum and 15-minute increments, a time range with crew count, the Save Your Ass prep speech she literally invited, and then 'we have September 2nd open — no deposit, want me to lock it in?' Also: introduce yourself by name in the first ten seconds — she had to ask who she'd been talking to for fifteen minutes.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently warm and unhurried with a customer who rambled — real empathy on the heirloom plant and the family history, and she ended the call sounding grateful — though his side leaned heavily on filler acknowledgments ('gotcha,' 'sure,' 'mm-hmm') and he never introduced himself by name.
audio_review_reason: The rep's turns are heavily garbled in the transcript ('we can just care about it,' 'I couldn't completely respect that I to'), so clarity and pace cannot be fairly judged from text — and the customer having to ask his name at the end may indicate an audio-level articulation issue rather than a scripting one.
